We subsequently retreated to the nearby Narayanhiti Gulm for safety, taking the office vehicles, weaponry, and most handheld sets with us. While we saved almost all vehicles and the majority of ammunition, a subsequent inventory revealed that some scattered weapons and ammunition had been looted. We later found that our office equipment, case files, uniforms, and personal belongings were either looted or burned. When we returned at 20:00 after the crowd dispersed, the office was uninhabitable. We spent that night inside the Narayanhiti premises with the Army. Throughout the 23rd and 24th, we only used verbal persuasion and baton charges; no other force was used, though the DSP and several personnel sustained minor injuries.
80. Statement of Senior Sub-Inspector Randhir Jaisi, working at the Crime Investigation Branch, Police Circle Balaju:

I have been working in the Crime Investigation Branch of Police Circle Balaju since June 2025. On September 8, 2025 (Bhadra 23), I was busy with internal administrative work within the branch. I had heard that the Gen-Z group was protesting in the Maitighar Mandala area regarding national interest, good governance, and anti-corruption. Per the security plan, a standby team was stationed at the circle while others were deployed for external duties. Later that day, I learned through social media that the situation at the Everest Hotel had turned uncontrollable, with protesters breaking barricades, entering prohibited areas, and vandalizing the Federal Parliament building. I also heard that several protesters died when police opened fire to stop the destruction, though I did not know the exact casualty count.

On the morning of September 9 (Bhadra 24), we were ordered to remain on standby in full uniform (Chusta). At around 07:00–08:00 AM, a team of 15–16 personnel, including myself and the Subedar Major, was securing the office. A crowd of 2,000 to 3,000 gathered at the gate, burning tires and chanting slogans. As the mob grew more aggressive, throwing stones and bottles, Inspector Dilip Kumar Humagain’s team arrived to assist. Protesters began throwing petrol bombs and using long sticks with flaming ends to ignite the office from over the boundary walls. We repeatedly extinguished fires using jars of water and fire extinguishers. When the crowd became chaotic, we used tear gas to disperse them and fired blanks as warning shots, as there were no orders to use lethal force. Eventually, the Circle Head's team returned from the field. I learned via social media that the President's residence and other private homes were also being attacked. During the struggle, a stone struck my leg, causing injury. The mob eventually set fire to the second floor of the barracks and the detention cells through the ventilators. Per orders received via radio to prioritize the safety of personnel and weaponry and to release detainees, we released 69 detainees whose remand had been extended and 5 others. To avoid a massive loss of life that would have resulted from final defensive force, we took as much weaponry and equipment as possible and retreated. Using blanks and tear gas to clear a path, we safely escorted our injured Circle Head and the team to the Nepal Army barracks in Nepaltar. I later learned through social media that two protesters were injured at Balaju and subsequently died during treatment.
81. Statement of Senior Sub-Inspector Jai Bahadur Singh, working at Police Circle Maharajgunj:

As the Subedar Major at Police Circle Maharajgunj, I am responsible for the deployment of personnel from Junior Police Officers downward. On September 8 and 9 (Bhadra 23–24), I remained at the office. On the 23rd, I learned through media that some protesters had died during the Gen-Z demonstrations. At that time, our Circle Head (DSP) was in the USA for departmental training. On the morning of the 24th, two of our Inspectors were deployed elsewhere by the District Police Range. Following reports that the Harisiddhi Police Division and other units were being burned, we merged smaller units into the circle, bringing our strength to about 40–45 personnel. Around 11:30 AM, a crowd of over 800 protesters began pelting the office with stones and petrol bombs, vowing to take revenge for the previous day's events. We heard reports that Balaju Circle, New Bus Park, and Tilingetar divisions had been burned and the mob was heading toward us. With no reinforcements available, we used tear gas and batons. By early afternoon, a massive influx of protesters from Balaju and the Bus Park arrived. Many police personnel were injured, and the mob breached the perimeter. While some of us tried to contain the fire, others tried to hold the gate. Per orders from 'Victor Control' to release detainees and secure weaponry and personnel, we attempted to evacuate. However, the fire spread rapidly, trapping some personnel who were forced to retreat to the roof, from where they were later rescued by a Nepal Army helicopter. Tragically, ASI Milan Rai and Constable Uttam Thapa were brutally murdered by the mob. Twenty-one personnel were seriously injured, and the office records and weaponry were either destroyed or looted.
82. Statement of Senior Sub-Inspector Shankar Prasad Chidi Magar, working at the Pashupati Temple Security Post:

Our primary duty is the security of the Pashupati Temple, while the outer perimeter is managed by the Armed Police Force (APF). No personnel from our post were deployed elsewhere on September 8 (Bhadra 23). On the 24th, following widespread reports of arson at Parliament, Singhadurbar, and private residences, we coordinated with the APF to secure the temple. While massive protests were visible in the surrounding area, we remained stationed within the temple premises. Protesters eventually set fire to the Pashupati Area Development Trust office near Gaushala. In the parking lot of that office, a motorcycle belonging to Police Constable Suraj Saud and two belonging to APF personnel were burned. No other loss of life or property occurred at our post; the personnel, weaponry, and documents of the Pashupati Temple Security Post remain safe.
83. Statement of Sub-Inspector Him Bahadur B.K., working at Police Circle Maharajgunj:

I serve as the head of the Logistics (Jinsi) Branch. On September 9 (Bhadra 24), I was ordered by the Subedar Major to assist with office security and was stationed at the main entrance. Around 10:00 AM, protesters began gathering at Narayan Gopal Chowk, Dhumbarahi, and Chundevi. Initially, it seemed like a peaceful protest, and we did not interfere. However, by 10:45 AM, we saw protesters carrying khukuris, swords, iron rods, hammers, and even SLR rifles. Construction stones piled on the Ring Road near Chundevi were used as missiles. Around 11:00 AM, the mob targeted the office with stones and petrol bombs. Government and private motorcycles, jeeps, and vans in the courtyard caught fire. Despite our use of tear gas, the sheer number of protesters allowed them to break the wire fencing and the main gate. They attacked us with sharp weapons and rods. I, along with several others, was beaten unconscious. While I was incapacitated with injuries to my head, forehead, and spine, the mob dragged ASI Milan Rai and Constable Uttam Thapa onto the street and brutally murdered them with sharp weapons. I was later informed that colleagues carried me to the roof, from where a Nepal Army helicopter rescued me and took me to the Nepal Police Hospital. Even though the police did not obstruct them that morning, the protesters intentionally targeted the office and committed murder. These individuals must face the maximum legal punishment.
84. Statement of Sub-Inspector Roshan Chand, working at Police Circle Swayambhu:

I am Sub-Inspector Roshan Chand of the Nepal Police, currently stationed at Police Circle Swayambhu since November 18, 2024, under the District Police Range Kathmandu. On September 8, 2025 (Bhadra 23), being assigned to the Investigation Branch, I was on standby at the office. I learned about the day's events through the duty officer and social media news updates. On September 9 (Bhadra 24), police teams from this office were deployed from the morning: one under the DSP to New Baneshwor, one under Inspector Janak Dhungana to Kalanki Chowk, and another under Inspector Dinesh Thapa to the CDO Office mode. About 30–35 personnel, including branch staff under Inspector Suraj Baniya, were assigned to office security. Around 11:30 AM, following reports of vandalism and arson at VIP residences in this office’s jurisdiction, a 10-member team under a Junior Police Officer was deployed to Sitapaila Chowk. By order of the higher office, the beat police also returned to this office around 12:00 PM. At approximately 12:15 PM, a small crowd initially arrived and attacked the police with stones; at that time, police and some locals attempted to persuade them to stop. Gradually, the group of protesters grew, and the situation became more aggressive and terrifying. Some individuals were seen carrying iron rods, khukuris, sticks, stones, and bottles filled with petrol. The Inspector repeatedly used a megaphone to appeal for calm, but the protesters ignored the requests and continued their attacks. While the office and personnel were under attack, we defended the office as per the commander's legal orders using sequential force: baton charges, tear gas, rubber cartridges from shotguns, and blank fires. Every effort was made to control the continuous attacks from the mob. Protesters attacked from all four sides, breaking walls and gates; 10–15 police personnel were injured. When they breached from the south and began vandalizing and setting fire to vehicles and assets around 2:30 PM (14:30), tear gas canisters were running out. Realizing the crowd could not be contained without live rounds, but following the Inspector's order that 'the office is not greater than human life' and to avoid human casualties, we decided to secure the weapons and important materials and move to a safe location. Since we could not exit the gate with the one-ton van containing weapons and case files, we carried as many weapons as possible and moved to the nearby Chhauni Military Hospital. That day, our team only used tear gas, rubber cartridges, and blank fires as per legal orders; no protesters were injured or killed by our actions. Police personnel were injured in the attack and are still undergoing treatment. The building, vehicles, weapons, case files, and personal belongings of the staff were completely destroyed by the protesters' vandalism and arson.
85. Statement of Sub-Inspector Dinesh Raut, working at Police Circle Maligaun:

On September 8, 2025 (Bhadra 23), being assigned to the Investigation Branch, I was on standby at the office. I learned about the day's events through the duty officer and social media news updates. On September 9 (Bhadra 24), a team was deployed to Baluwatar under the DSP and to Baneshwor Chowk under Inspector Dawa Tenji Sherpa, while about 20–25 personnel remained for office security under Inspector Ajay Jung Thapa. Around 11:30 AM, after receiving reports of attacks on police beats and VIP houses in our area, beat police were recalled to the office by 12:00 PM by order of the higher office. Around 1:15 PM, the Circle Head also returned to the office for security. Shortly after, a crowd of 200–300 people arrived, which gradually grew more aggressive and terrifying. Some carried iron rods, khukuris, sticks, stones, and petrol bombs, and began pelting stones at the police. Commanders formed a cordon on both sides of the road and used megaphones to appeal to the protesters, but they ignored the requests and continued attacking. As the office and personnel were attacked, we followed the commander's legal orders, using sequential persuasion, baton charges, tear gas, rubber cartridges, and blank fires to disperse the mob 3–4 times. No damage occurred at this office. Our team used only tear gas, rubber cartridges, and blank fires as per legal orders; no protesters were injured or killed.
86. Statement of Assistant Sub-Inspector Rajan Karki, working at Police Circle Gaushala:

I am Assistant Sub-Inspector Rajan Karki. On September 8, 2025 (Bhadra 23), I was on regular duty at the office. On the 24th, I was on office security duty under Inspector Uddhav Pokharel. From early morning on the 24th, all personnel were at their assigned posts. Around 10:00 AM, Gen-Z protesters began appearing at Chabahil Chowk, Gaushala Chowk, and Runche Danda. They were chanting slogans and making noise. Initially, we thought it was a peaceful protest, and the police did not interfere. Around 11:00 AM, about 6,000–7,000 protesters targeted the office with khukuris, iron rods, slingshots, stones, and petrol bombs. Police protected themselves and the office from the missiles. The protesters intensified the use of petrol bombs, setting fire to government and private motorcycles, jeeps, and vans in the courtyard.

87. Statement of Assistant Sub-Inspector Pramod Kumar Yadav, working at the Federal Parliament Security Base, Baneshwor:

The Federal Parliament Security Base is under the command of an Inspector. There are high-point posts around the building where duty is rotated 24 hours a day with INSAS rifles. This is a prohibited area where protests are not allowed. Additional security from the Nepal Police and Armed Police Force is deployed during sessions or protests. On September 8, 2025 (Bhadra 23), there was a Gen-Z protest for national interest and governance, and a National Assembly meeting was also scheduled. Accordingly, additional security was deployed.

I was at the south VIP gate in full gear, unarmed; teams from the Nepal Police and APF were also there. Around 11:00 AM, thousands of protesters breached the prohibited area, surrounded the building, and attempted to enter by breaking walls and gates. Security personnel tried to persuade them, but they became anarchic and continued their attempts. They attacked the high posts with stones and vandalized gates and police posts. The mob turned into a riot and began committing arson. Security forces had batons, gas guns, INSAS, and SLRs. As the riot escalated, the APF used gas guns and later blank fires when the situation wasn't controlled. This continued periodically throughout the day. Many police were injured by stones. In the evening, after the crowd was contained, I learned through Facebook and social media about injuries and deaths among protesters. An Army team also arrived for security. On the morning of the 24th, the Army, APF, and Nepal Police were securing the building. Protests by the Gen-Z group continued from all sides. Around 1:00 PM (13:00), an overwhelming number of protesters gathered, targeting the building with stones, slingshots, and petrol bombs. They used tools like pickaxes to break the perimeter walls and entered with khukuris and spears, eventually setting the Parliament building on fire. We then secured our weapons and ammunition. On the 24th, the Nepal Army did not play any protective role as the protesters burned the building.
88. Statement of Assistant Sub-Inspector Pradip Singh Dhami, working at the Valley Police Office, Ranipokhari, Kathmandu:

I work in the Logistics (Management) Branch at the Kathmandu Valley Police Office, Ranipokhari. During the Gen-Z protests on September 8 and 9, 2025 (Bhadra 23 and 24), I was not deployed in the field. This office primarily commands Kathmandu, Bhaktapur, and Lalitpur and issues directions. Until September 8, DIG Om Bahadur Rana was the acting chief.

I learned that then-AIG Dan Bahadur Karki (current IGP) was to be deployed from the 24th. Personnel at this office are usually busy with internal administrative work rather than field duty. Following the casualties on the 23rd, protesters were aggressively vandalizing and burning sites from the morning of the 24th. Reports arrived of police offices being attacked and weapons being looted. Reinforcements from other offices were impossible. Office-based staff then organized local security. Arson was occurring at VIP residences, police offices, Singhadurbar, and Parliament. I asked then-SSP (now DIG) Shekhar Khanal about managing the weapons in the logistics branch; he told me to report to acting chief DIG Om Bahadur Rana and not to panic. Around 2:00–3:00 PM, a large group armed with sticks, spears, pickaxes, shovels, slingshots, and khukuris attacked the office. There was a dual challenge of protecting the office and weapons while avoiding casualties among the protesters. We tried to persuade them, but they entered the premises, creating an environment where no one could be heard. I am unaware of what specific commands were issued. Personnel began getting injured: Senior Head Constable Amrit Kumar Shrestha suffered a leg injury, and Head Constable Ram Krishna Dhungana’s leg was broken. Personnel then prioritized their own safety. No one had the chance to focus on the building or weaponry. Protesters took that opportunity to set fire to vehicles and the building and took away weapons. The following weapons have not been recovered yet.
89. Statement of Police Assistant Sub-Inspector Hareram Kumal, serving at Police Division Koteshwar:

On Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082, during demonstrations by the Gen-Z youth generation in Kathmandu and various parts of the country, I was on standby duty at the office on the 23rd. On the 24th, I was deployed as duty officer at Police Division Koteshwar. At approximately 10:30 AM that day while I was in the duty officer's room, a group of 400–500 people came and attempted to attack the office and us. Locals from Koteshwar Chowk joined hands and persuaded the crowd that they should not set fire to the police office or beat police, and sent them toward Tinkune Baneswhar. After that, at around 11:00 AM, a mob coming from the Koteshwar overpass went to the Koteshwar Traffic Office, vandalized it, and set it on fire. Shortly after, that mob came to the gate of Police Division Koteshwar, threw stones, and hurled petrol bombs from outside, which we extinguished twice. At around 12:30, a mob of approximately 3,000–4,000 came to the gate outside Police Division Koteshwar, threw stones, and threatened from outside: 'Either come out of the office or we will burn you alive inside.' After they began attacking, we were forced to flee. As the crowd attacked from all four sides simultaneously and resistance and self-defense became impossible, police colleagues fled in all directions to save their lives. I too fled, entered a lane to the north of Police Division Koteshwar, entered a local resident's home, and hid in a small room like a storage room. During the attack by the agitators that day, some parts of my body were struck by stones, batons, bricks, kicks, and punches, but I was not seriously injured. My health condition is currently normal. I do not recognize any of the people who were attacking at that time. The statement I have given to the best of my knowledge is true and accurate.
90. Statement of Police Assistant Sub-Inspector Khemraj Adhikari, serving at Police Circle Kirtipur, Kathmandu:

I have been serving at Police Circle Kirtipur since 2081/12/06. On Bhadra 23, 2082, I was doing regular work at the Crime Investigation Branch of my own office. Even while working at the branch, I was aware of the immediate situation of the movement, and for that reason I was also troubled thinking about the next day's events and the state of peace, security, and order. I could not sleep that night because of those thoughts. Despite not sleeping until late at night, on the 24th I got up early in the morning, completed my daily routine, gathered information about the current situation, received crowd control equipment and weapons, took orders from my then-commander DSP Raj Babu Maharjan, and was processing case work related to persons detained in custody on drug-related offenses on the 23rd. At around 11:00 AM, a group of approximately 1,000–1,200 demonstrators came and attempted to stone-throw at the office, whereupon the then-commander DSP Raj Babu Maharjan persuaded the group of agitators and sent them away. The situation was normal for a while, but information was also received that arson and vandalism had occurred at various locations in Kirtipur. At around 12:00 noon, a group of 3,000–4,000 agitators again came, entered the office, and attempted stone-throwing, arson, and looting. Under the orders of Commander DSP Raj Babu Maharjan, persuasion was attempted and graduated crowd control measures were adopted as much as possible to the point where shooting would have been required, but as per supervisory office orders and considering the immediate situation of minimizing human casualties  since firing would cause excessive human casualties  we were deployed to protect the office and its materials to the extent possible. At that point, a group of aggressive, lawless anarchists entered the office compound from all four sides and completely damaged the office and police barracks through vandalism, looting, and arson. While we were still requesting them not to commit arson, we took our weapons and went to a safe location. The entire day passed in a state of fear and terror. Even in such circumstances, due to the skilled leadership and situational assessment ability of Commander DSP Raj Babu Maharjan, no human casualties occurred, and as a result the days following were easier for daily police operations and there was a positive effect on police morale. This statement is true and accurate.
91. Statement of Police Assistant Sub-Inspector Birendra Singh Bista, serving at Nepal Police Indefinite Battalion, Dillibazar:

During the movement by the Generation Z group on Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082, on Bhadra 24, 2082, at approximately 16:30, a group of 400–500 people attacked the Dillibazar Prison, broke the main gate of Nepal Police Indefinite Battalion Dillibazar, entered inside, committed arson at the line barracks, and entered the DIA room, vandalizing and damaging communication equipment, CCTV cameras, and monitors. Even after police made public address announcements and persuaded them, they did not comply. After using necessary force to send that group out of the prison perimeter, members of that same group set fire to buses outside and again committed arson at the line barracks. At around 20:30, after pushing the agitators back, we were successful in keeping 669 prisoners of various categories safely inside the prison. On the morning of Bhadra 25, 2082, at approximately 8:30 AM, prisoners inside Dillibazar Prison  having learned that prisoners in other prisons had been released  demanded that they too should be released and began protests and slogan-chanting from 8:30 AM. Immediately reporting to the supervisory Nepal Police Deval and Kathmandu Valley Police Victor Control and requesting additional support, the prisoners were addressed via public address. In the course of this, when prisoners attempted to break the inner main gate and exit, the team under the command of Nepal Police Indefinite Battalion Dillibazar's Police Durga Rai and a Nepali Army team successfully persuaded all prisoners to return inside the prison. Thereafter, after prisoners committed vandalism and arson inside the prison and attempted to escape from all four sides, the deployed team immediately transferred 458 prisoners to the Central Prison, and 192 prisoners including the head warden were managed to remain at Dillibazar Prison. Of these, 20 prisoners in various cases escaped and are at large  10 have since been brought back and 10 remain fugitives and are being searched for by their respective supervisory offices. This is true and accurate.
92. Statement of Police Assistant Sub-Inspector Prakash Ray, serving at Police Circle Lainchaur:

During demonstrations by the Gen-Z youth generation in Kathmandu and various parts of the country on Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082, on Bhadra 23 I was deployed at 8:30 AM under the command of Police Circle Lainchaur Office Chief Deputy Superintendent of Police Jageshwar Bhandari with a team of 15 personnel in the northern lane of Alpha Beta in Baneswhar, and on Bhadra 24 I was deployed from 9:00 AM in cordon duty in front of Ascol Campus in Lainchaur.

On Bhadra 23, I was deployed at 8:30 AM under the command of Police Circle Lainchaur Office Chief DSP Jageshwar Bhandari with a team of 15 personnel in the main barricade duty in the northern lane of Alpha Beta in Baneswhar. From approximately 10:00 AM, people had already begun gathering. Most of those who gathered were youth and young women in what appeared to be school and college uniforms. They were raising various slogans against the government. After that, at around 11:00 AM, a crowd of 7,000–8,000 people from Maitighar Mandala merged with the crowd already present. As the crowd reached the barricade and numbers increased, it became increasingly agitated and aggressive. The crowd chanted slogans for some time, and after a while began pushing, kicking, and targeting the barricade. My team was deployed in the front line of the barricade and we made tireless efforts for a long time to keep the barricade from collapsing. During this, our commander made announcements for a long time requesting peaceful demonstration, but the crowd's agitation and aggression did not stop. After holding the barricade for approximately 40 minutes to one hour, the force of the immense crowd collapsed the barricade toward us. Even after the barricade fell, my team and I tried to stop the crowd by forming a barricade with our batons. Despite tireless efforts, the crowd advanced toward the Parliament Building and my team was falling back. While falling back, the crowd became further aggressive toward us and began hurling stones, bricks, water bottles, and helmets at us. Even when Nepal Police's water cannon sprayed water at the crowd, the crowd did not retreat. My team, protecting itself with shields, took duty toward Gate No. 2 of the Federal Parliament Building. Even after taking duty toward Gate No. 2 of the Federal Parliament Building, stones, bricks, water bottles, and helmets continued to be hurled at us. By this time, no sound of gunfire was heard from anywhere. After approximately one hour of continuous projectile attacks, as our numbers were small, we moved inside from Gate No. 2 of the Federal Parliament Building. After we went inside, Gate No. 2 of the Federal Parliament Building was fully locked with an iron chain. Some time later, an enraged crowd made a hole in the wall on the side of the Citizen Investment Fund gate and approximately 8–10 demonstrators entered, whereupon my team took up baton charge positions and chased those who had entered back out.

Some time later, the crowd grew more aggressive and set fire to a single-story building near Gate No. 2. After the arson, my commander's team fired several rounds of tear gas toward the crowd, used sand to partially suppress the fire, then went back outside the gate and dispersed the crowd. After that, demonstrators set fire to four vehicles, the office motorcycles, and personal vehicles of police personnel at Police Circle Janasewa  they were burned and destroyed  and police personnel were hit with stones and sustained minor injuries. At around 5 PM, demonstrators completely set fire to the police office where I serve.
100. Statement of Police Assistant Constable Laxman Raj Jaisi, serving at Police Circle New Baneswhar, Kathmandu:

While demonstrations were happening in various parts of the country, on Bhadra 23 and 24 I was on duty at the office for office security. On both days, demonstrators had thrown stones at the office. On Bhadra 24, 2082, from 7:00 AM, 25–30 police personnel including myself were deployed for office security under the command of Police Inspector Ramesh Rai. In the morning, demonstrators numbering 1,000–1,200 repeatedly threw stones at the office, and in the afternoon a group of 4,000–5,000 demonstrators came carrying looted weapons from elsewhere, plastic bottles filled with kerosene, diesel, and petrol and other flammable substances, sharp weapons, iron rods, bricks, stones, and batons, and threw stones and bricks from outside at the Police Circle New Baneswhar office building where I was deployed. Even after we repeatedly fired tear gas and aerial rounds to stop the crowd, the agitated crowd entered the office, and the Armed Police Force unit nearby also left that location, so demonstrators broke through the main gate and entered the office. Per orders not to cause human casualties, we were compelled not to use force for the safety of people's lives. As a result, demonstrators  taking advantage of police not using force  entered the police office, sprinkled flammable substances including kerosene, diesel, and petrol, hurled petrol bombs, set fire to vehicles in the office parking and the office building, completely destroying everything. After that, the police team deployed for office security was unable to stop the agitated crowd, and we went to the nearby 7.5 Niketan School for a safe location. Agitators also came to that school, forcibly made police personnel including myself remove our uniforms, lined us up, and attacked with iron rods, sharp weapons, bricks, stones, punches, and kicks  chasing and beating us  and took us 100 meters ahead to under the Bagmati River bridge with the intent to kill, physically tortured us, forcibly pushed us into the Bagmati River, and from both banks ruthlessly pelted bricks and stones, beating us mercilessly until we were near death, seriously injuring us. Several police personnel including myself were injured in that incident. I was injured in that incident and was admitted for 1 day at Civil Service Hospital in Baneswhar and 6 days at Nepal Police Hospital in Maharajgunj for treatment. In that incident, I sustained deep injuries to my head and various parts of my body. Demonstrators vandalized the police office and committed arson and looting of weapons, ammunition, cash, and other goods in the office. The above statement is true and accurate.
101. Statement of Police Assistant Constable Ganesh Khadka, serving at Police Division Koteshwar:

My name is Ganesh Khadka. I am currently 34 years old. My grandfather's name is Hari Bahadur Khadka and my father's name is Chakra Bahadur Khadka. My district is Dolakha, Gaurishankar Rural Municipality, Ward No. 5. I currently live with my family in a rented room in Sanepа, Lalitpur. I joined the police service on Chaitra 25, 2069, and have been serving at Police Division Koteshwar for the past six months. During demonstrations by the Gen-Z youth generation in Kathmandu and various parts of the country on Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082, I was deployed on duty in the ward area of Police Division Koteshwar. On Bhadra 23, 2082, I was deployed on duty at Police Division Koteshwar, Kathmandu under the command of Police Sub-Inspector Indra Bahadur Basnet for office security. On Bhadra 24, under the command of Police Sub-Inspector Indra Bahadur Basnet for the security of Koteshwar Chowk and Police Division Koteshwar  at approximately 11:00 AM, as agitators began attacking police from all four sides with stones, bricks, petrol bombs, and batons, we fell back and entered the office compound. After that, as they began attempting to set fire to the office, while requesting the crowd to move some distance away and coming outside to persuade them, an agitated group attacked me along with others from all four sides with stones, bricks, khukuris, and spears  causing the body protector, helmet, and shield I was wearing to break. When the crowd attacked to the point where resistance and self-defense became impossible, all police personnel began fleeing in all directions to save their lives. I too fled and entered the Bhrikuti Bhawan next to Police Division, saving my life. I did not know where the others went  inside Bhrikuti Bhawan I had approximately 15–16 colleagues, some of whom were injured while others were unharmed. My current condition is normal. I do not recognize any of the people who were attacking at that time. The statement I have given to the best of my knowledge is true and accurate.
102. Statement of Police Assistant Constable Rudra Prasad Gautam, serving at Police Division Koteshwar:

During demonstrations by the Gen-Z youth generation in Kathmandu and various parts of the country on Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082, I was deployed as the duty officer's assistant at Police Division Koteshwar. On Bhadra 23, I was deployed on duty at Police Division Koteshwar, Kathmandu under the command of Police Sub-Inspector Indra Bahadur Basnet for office security. On Bhadra 24, deployed as duty officer's assistant under the command of Police Assistant Sub-Inspector Hareram Kumal  at approximately 10:30 AM, when a group of 400–500 came and attempted to attack the office and us, locals from Koteshwar Chowk joined hands and persuaded the crowd that they should not commit arson at the police office or beat police, and sent them toward Tinkune Baneswhar. At around 11:00 AM, a mob coming from the Koteshwar overpass went to the Koteshwar Traffic Office, vandalized it, set it on fire, and shortly afterward that mob came to the gate of Police Division Koteshwar, threw stones, and hurled petrol bombs from outside, which we extinguished twice. At approximately 12:30, a mob of approximately 3,000–4,000 came to the gate outside Police Division Koteshwar, threw stones, threatened from outside  'Either come out of the office or we will burn you alive inside'  and began attacking. Being forced to flee, I and 5–6 colleagues fled along the sidewalk on the left side of our office and entered a local's home, going up 4–5 floors and locking ourselves inside a room from within. After that mob burned the office and came to where we were staying, they broke the door from outside and entered. As soon as they entered, I broke the glass window of that room and went outside, jumped from that building to another building, landing in a flower garden where I stayed. Within 10–15 minutes of having escaped from that room, a group of 25–30 people found me and said 'this one must die'  they grabbed me, dragged me by the feet down from the roof of that building, struck my head with bricks, batons, and kicks on the way down, after which I became semi-conscious. I was thrown from the roof of that building to the edge of the sidewalk below. I vaguely remember some people saying 'kill this one,' others saying 'this one is dead, leave him,' and some saying 'let's throw him in the hospital.' After being beaten on the sidewalk I fell into unconsciousness, and a local woman said 'this is the brother from Koteshwar, I know him'  that woman sent me to KMC Hospital in Sinamangal. When I regained consciousness on the 24th, I was in a bed at Kathmandu Medical College in Sinamangal. My current condition is normal. I do not recognize any of the people who were attacking at that time.
103. Statement of Police Assistant Constable Yogendra Bahadur Chand, serving at Police Circle Kalimati:

On Bhadra 23, 2082, I was deployed on duty at the Crime Investigation Branch inside the office. No incident occurred within my responsibility that day and duty was completed normally. From 7:00 AM on Bhadra 24, 2082, I was again on duty at that same branch. At approximately 8:00 AM that morning, information came through the police control room communication set that some agitators were burning tires and demonstrating at Kalankhi Chowk, Ward No. 14, Kathmandu Metropolitan City, Kathmandu district. At that time, a police team under Police Inspector Bijayraj Timalsina of this same office went to that location, while police personnel at the office including myself were deployed at the main gate of Police Circle Kalimati for office security. Some time later, DSP Madhu Kumar Thapa  who had been injured in the Gen-Z movement at Baneswhar on the 23rd and was staying at this office while receiving treatment  took additional medication and a pain-reducing injection and immediately went with an additional team toward Kalankhi Chowk despite being injured. At approximately 10:00 AM that morning, approximately 100 demonstrators raising slogans passed through the road in front of this Police Circle toward Kalimati Chowk. Approximately 30 minutes later, approximately 4,000–5,000 demonstrators came carrying weapons to the office gate and raised slogans: 'Police shot and killed people in Baneswhar on the 23rd, these people must also be killed, burn them alive.' Kathmandu Valley Police Control Room at Bhadrakali broadcast instructions through communication sets not to use much force, not to fire live rounds, and to act with restraint to prevent further human casualties  so we sat defensively, repeatedly making public address announcements urging the crowd to remain calm, but nobody listened and continuous attacks on police began. The demonstrators surrounded all four sides of this Police Circle, throwing stones, bricks, and petrol bombs. DSP Madhu Kumar Thapa and his police team arrived at this office, and a police team under 2 Police Inspectors deployed from Municipal Police Office Bhrikuti Mandap also arrived. After that, we fired tear gas and dispersed the crowd, entered the circle, and removed 300–400 demonstrators who were inside. After thousands of demonstrators coming from Kalankhi direction and demonstrators from Balkhu direction and demonstrators in Kalimati all met, the situation went beyond control. Smoke from fires on the roads and at police offices rose in all directions. Demonstrators from Balkhu direction arrived on motorcycles carrying shotguns, 303 rifles, and SLRs; some demonstrators were wearing police uniforms. When a strong team from Police Circle Kalimati and municipal police tried to stop demonstrators at the gate, as they could not enter through the gate, they went into buildings on the right, left, and rear and threw petrol bombs from rooftops. This caused the rooms on the front road-facing side of the Police Circle to catch fire. The traffic building at the rear also caught fire, and vans of traffic police parked on the side, other vehicles, and the traffic police van at this office gate also caught fire. As armed demonstrators entered through the main gate of the circle and tried to seize a shotgun and ammunition from police and take over other weapons, repeated public address announcements were made by police and some dummy rounds were fired aerially for self-defense. As demonstrators on motorcycles and minivans from Balaju and Swayambhu direction arrived shouting that all police must be killed and tried to enter the circle, when the circle started burning and even public address announcements were not heeded, after aerial fire, demonstrators retreated somewhat  seizing that opportunity, detainees in this circle's custody were released temporarily for life preservation purposes per the office chief's orders with notification to the supervisory office, telling them to appear later. After Kathmandu Valley Police Control at Bhadrakali informed that all personnel should leave the office and take weapons, communication sets, and vehicles to a safe location to prevent further human casualties, all weapons and communication sets were loaded into a police van and personnel went via Kalimati Chowk, Teku, Shahid Gate to Bhadrakali Range. My police team along with others was also pelted with stones on the way. Despite requesting additional support repeatedly, we received information that additional support from other security agencies could not come and to keep ourselves safe. Later, as thousands of demonstrators came to Bhadrakali Range carrying weapons to attack, after public address announcements were not heeded, some rounds of tear gas and dummy round aerial fire were used, which prevented arson and looting at Bhadrakali Range. We acted per orders of the commander deployed for security at the District Police Range. There were dozens of attempts to attack the District Police Range. At approximately 19:30, as demonstrators coming on more than 100 motorcycles and in Armed Police Force trucks tried to ram a truck into the gate to break it, we stopped them with tear gas and baton charges. All kinds of people were involved in the attacks that day  mostly drug users, those working at transportation counters in the Kalankhi-Balkhu area, laborers, squatter settlement residents, scrap workers of Indian origin, and detainees who had escaped from police custody  I estimate. I cannot say for certain who exactly joined together. After our police team left the circle, arson and looting occurred at Kalimati Circle, completely damaging all materials, furniture, and personal vehicles of police personnel in all branches. All vehicles in this office compound were completely damaged by arson. A shotgun and ammunition were looted from this office  the shotgun has since been recovered but the ammunition has not yet been found. In that incident, 60–65 police personnel from this office were injured, and some demonstrators were also injured from baton charges. I don't have the exact number of those. Police personnel were injured from attacks and beatings by demonstrators, while demonstrators were injured from police baton charges and in the course of fleeing. As per orders from the supervisory office, we used minimum force and saved weapons, communication sets, and police vans at risk to our own lives. In that incident, personal vehicles and all belongings of police personnel including myself were burned and destroyed.
104. Statement of Police Constable Ashok Kumar Awasthi, serving at Police Circle Kirtipur:

On Bhadra 23, 2082, I was doing regular work at the Crime Investigation Branch of my own office. Even while working at the branch, I was aware of the immediate situation of the movement. For that reason, I was troubled thinking about the next day's events and the state of peace, security, and order in the country. Despite various thoughts disturbing my mind until late that night, while thinking about the next day's security, I fell asleep without realizing it. Getting up early the next morning, completing my daily routine, and understanding the current situation, as we were about to go to the mess for food, everyone suddenly took their equipment and under orders from Commander DSP Raj Babu Maharjan  at approximately 11:00 AM, a group of approximately 1,000–1,200 demonstrators came and attempted to stone-throw at the office, whereupon Commander DSP Raj Babu Maharjan persuaded the group of agitators and sent them away. The situation was normal for a while, but information was also received that arson and vandalism had occurred at various locations in Kirtipur. At approximately 12:00 noon, a group of 3,000–4,000 agitators again came, entered the office, and attempted stone-throwing, arson, and looting. Under Commander DSP Raj Babu Maharjan's orders, persuasion was attempted and graduated crowd control measures were adopted as much as possible to the point where shooting would have been required, but as per supervisory office orders and considering the immediate situation of minimizing human casualties  since firing would cause excessive human casualties  we were deployed to protect the office and its materials to the extent possible. At that point, a group of aggressive, lawless anarchists entered the office compound from all four sides and completely damaged the office and police barracks through vandalism, looting, and arson. While still requesting them not to commit arson, we took our weapons and went to a safe location. The entire day passed in a state of fear and terror. Even in such circumstances, due to the skilled leadership and situational assessment ability of Commander DSP Raj Babu Maharjan, no human casualties occurred, and as a result, the days following were easier for daily police operations and there was a positive effect on police morale. This is true and accurate.
105. Statement of Police Constable Manoj Gyawali, serving at Parliament Building Security Base, Baneswhar:

High Point Posts are maintained on all four sides of the Federal Parliament Building, and personnel are deployed at those posts around the clock on rotating duty with INSAS rifles. That area is a restricted zone where activities such as sit-ins and demonstrations are prohibited. On days when Parliament sessions are in session at the Federal Parliament Building, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force also come for additional security. On Bhadra 23, 2082, my duty was at High Post No. 14 on the Baneswhar Chowk side of the Federal Parliament Building from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM with an INSAS rifle and 36 rounds of ammunition. As the National Assembly session was also being held that day, additional security from Nepal Police and Armed Police Force had also arrived. I was on my own duty. At approximately 11:00 or 11:30, thousands of demonstrators from all four sides, growing agitated, surrounded the Parliament Building and attempted to break walls and doors and enter the Parliament Building. Immediately, additional support from Nepal Police and Armed Police Force arrived and began persuading the demonstrators. Demonstrators did not listen to police and became more anarchic, breaking and vandalizing the Parliament Building and attempting to enter. In the course of this, they came near my post and chanting 'attack attack' began throwing stones at me. After stone-throwing began, I came out from my post with my weapon and fell back. Demonstrators began vandalizing the Parliament Building entrance gate and police posts. Sounds of gas gun and bullet fire from outside began to be heard. I did not fire my weapon. In the evening, the crowd went to their respective destinations and things calmed down. After it calmed down, I learned through Facebook and various social media that demonstrators had been injured and had died. That evening, a Nepali Army team also came and began providing security for the Federal Parliament Building. On the following day, the 24th, from the morning, Nepal Army, Armed Police Force, Nepal Police, and police personnel from the Federal Parliament Building Security Base Baneswhar were all providing security for the Federal Parliament Building. That day I had no weapon with me  I was in crowd control attire with a baton. That day too, the Gen-Z generation was conducting an all-around movement. A large group of demonstrators had surrounded the Parliament Building from all four sides and was demonstrating. While demonstrators were demonstrating and security police were continuing to persuade them, at approximately 13:00, an uncontrollable large number gathered around the Parliament Building and targeted it with stone-throwing, slingshots, and petrol bombs and other flammable substances  injuring many police  broke through the Parliament Building compound walls using pickaxes and similar tools, and entered the Parliament Building compound brandishing khukuris while creating commotion, and set fire to the Parliament Building. After that, we secured our weapons and ammunition.
106. Statement of Police Constable Jitendra Mahat, serving at Police Circle Balaju:

On Bhadra 23, 2082, from 2:00 PM I was deployed as additional support duty at Shital Niwas gate outside the Presidential Palace under the command of Police Circle Balaju Chief DSP Gyan Bahadur Bista. The situation was normal at my deployed location that day, but in the evening, Gen-Z movement people on motorcycles were spitting at police and engaging in verbal abuse. That day, Gen-Z group members were demonstrating and moving at Maitighar Mandala area demanding national interest, good governance, and corruption control, and in the evening I learned through social media that shots had been fired as they tried to vandalize and set fire to the Parliament Building, resulting in the death of some demonstrators. The next day as well, I was deployed on vehicle duty under DSP Gyan Bahadur Bista's command. We were on duty in the ward area of Police Circle Balaju. First arriving at Kharibot, I saw many people gathered there. None of the demonstrators were in school uniforms. Those gathered came to Banasthali Chowk and were burning tires and demonstrating. The crowd was extremely large. The crowd began throwing stones and setting fire to the Banasthali Police Post. As we had few personnel, nothing other than persuasion could be done. After that, upon hearing rumors that the crowd might set fire to the President's private residence in Bohora, our team went toward the President's private residence. Demonstrators came toward the President's private residence carrying bamboo batons, bottles, stones, and petrol bombs. We had no personnel other than the vehicle team. When we tried to persuade the demonstrators, the crowd became more aggressive and anarchic. After persuasion did not work, we tried to disperse the crowd with tear gas and rubber bullets. The crowd did not comply. As the crowd was extremely large, they came back and attacked police, and began arson, looting, and vandalism at the President's private residence. Using firearms would likely have caused large numbers of demonstrators to be hit. After that, when orders came through the communication set to protect ourselves and the office, we walked back toward the office with the help of locals. The DSP had already sent the vehicle to the office at the beginning fearing it might be vandalized. Upon arriving at the office, no demonstrators were around Balaju Circle in school uniforms. Approximately 2,000–3,000 demonstrators gathered at the office gate, raised slogans, and began burning tires at the gate demonstrating. After some in the crowd began throwing stones, we tried to persuade them. The crowd of demonstrators kept coming from various locations and lanes. When we arrived at our office, demonstrators were already vandalizing the office. Commanders tried to persuade the crowd, but they became even more aggressive and the entire office had already been completely vandalized. Demonstrators repeatedly threw petrol bombs while some used fire torches on long batons to set fire inside the office from outside the wall. Many times we extinguished the fires with water from jars and fire extinguishers. As they also threw fire at vehicles from outside, we extinguished those fires many times. After that, we fired aerial fire and tear gas, dispersed the demonstrators, and though the office was vandalized, we were preventing arson. This process of protecting the office kept repeating many times. Demonstrators threw stones and set fires from all four sides. A petrol bomb thrown by demonstrators hit the office chief's body, and he was also hit by stones and seriously injured. As the crowd of demonstrators kept growing, we were making aerial fire and blank round fire to try to disperse them. As this repeated many times, the situation began going beyond control. Thousands of demonstrators pelted stones and set fire to the second floor of the barracks from behind; gradually from the front they set fire through the detention room ventilation window. As smoke started coming from the detention cell and arson began at various locations of the office, demonstrators entered the office and tried to loot materials. We were trying to stop them. Finally, carrying as many weapons and equipment as possible, firing aerial shots with blank rounds and tear gas while dispersing the crowd, we went and stayed at the Nepali Army barracks at Nepaltar. During stone-throwing and arson at Police Circle Balaju, 2 demonstrators were injured and taken for treatment, and I heard through social media that they died during treatment. I don't know how or why they died.
107. Statement of Police Constable Kshetraraj Timalsena, serving at Police Circle Swayambhu:

On Bhadra 23, 2082, since I was serving at the Supply Branch, I was on standby at the office that day. I learned about the events of that day after the duty officer informed me and news came through social media. On Bhadra 24, 2082, a police team went from this office from the morning  under DSP's command to New Baneswhar, under Police Inspector Janak G's command to Kalankhi Chowk, and under Police Inspector Dinesh Thapa's command to the CDO Office junction. For office security, there were 30–35 personnel including branch staff under Police Inspector Suraj Bania's command. At approximately 11:30 AM that day, upon receiving information that VIP residences in this office's ward area had been vandalized and set on fire, a team of 10 under a junior officer's command was deployed to Sitapaila Chowk. Per higher office orders, beat police also returned to this office at 12:00 noon. At approximately 12:15 PM, some people first came and threw stones at police and attacked, and police along with some locals tried to stop the attack through persuasion. As the group of demonstrators gradually grew and the situation became more aggressive and terrifying  some individuals carrying rods and khukuris, some seen carrying batons, stones, chunks of concrete, and petrol-filled bottles  the Police Inspector repeatedly made public address announcements requesting and persuading demonstrators, but demonstrators disregarded this and continued attacking continuously. As police and the office came under attack, following the commander's legal orders  graduated baton charge, tear gas, shotgun rubber cartridges, and aerial fire as needed  office security was maintained. Every effort was made to control the continuous attacks from groups of demonstrators. As demonstrators pelted stones from all four sides and broke through walls and the gate, 10–15 police were also injured. As they entered from the south side and began vandalism and arson at vehicles and the barracks, at approximately 14:30, as tear gas shells were running out and the crowd could not be contained without firing live rounds, the Police Inspector ordered 'do not fire live rounds  people's lives are more important than the office.' With the aim of preventing human casualties, we took the weapons and important materials and went to a safe location. When trying to take case files and weapons in a one-ton vehicle, it was not possible to get out through the gate, so we took as many weapons as we could carry and went to the nearby Military Hospital Chhauni. On that day as well, from our team, per legal orders, only tear gas shells for crowd control, shotgun rubber cartridges, and live bullets for aerial fire were used, and no demonstrators were injured and no human casualties occurred. This is true and accurate. Police personnel were injured from demonstrators' attacks and are still receiving treatment. The office building, vehicles, weapons, case files, supply materials, and personal clothing and belongings of police personnel were all completely burned and destroyed by demonstrators' vandalism and arson. This is true and accurate.

109. Statement of Police Constable Chuman Singh Dhami, serving at Police Circle Thankot:

During demonstrations by the Gen-Z youth generation in Kathmandu and various parts of the country on Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082, on Bhadra 23 I was deployed at Maitighar Mandala at approximately 10:00 AM under the command of Police Circle Thankot's DSP Eliza Giri with a team of 15 personnel, and on Bhadra 24 I was deployed for Police Circle Thankot security from 4:00 AM under DSP Eliza Giri's command with a team of 35 personnel for office security  other police personnel from the office were on regular mobile and other duties, and a police team under 2 Police Inspectors was deployed as additional support outside the office. On Bhadra 23, under DSP Eliza Giri's command with a team of 15 personnel, I had taken duty in full gear at Maitighar Mandala at approximately 10:00 AM. At that time, approximately 1,000 people had gathered at Maitighar, and some of those gathered were in school and college uniforms. Those gathered were raising slogans that demonstrations would be peaceful and non-disruptive. After that, the number of people gathering at Maitighar Mandala kept increasing and must have reached 10,000–12,000. While gathering, various individuals were making speeches, and we were on duty in positions to cordon off the crowd. Between approximately 11:30 and 12:00, the crowd that had gathered at Maitighar Mandala walked toward New Baneswhar, and some people were also riding in an open pickup truck making announcements. The crowd moving forward was getting more agitated and it was quite difficult for our team including myself to cordon it off while keeping pace. Most of the people present in the crowd were in the youth age group and they were not prepared to listen to our requests. As we advanced, when the crowd reached the Road Department area, it began moving forward while blocking the entire road and not allowing vehicle traffic. As we advanced further and the crowd reached the Thapagaun bridge, when our team tried to take it via only the left-side road while cordoning it, the crowd became further enraged, verbally abusing police with obscene words while taking up the entire road and advancing. After that, the crowd reached the barricade in front of Everest Hotel where there was also an additional police team, and up until reaching there our team including myself had been cordoning the crowd from the front. After that, our team was behind the barricade while the crowd was raising abusive slogans and chanting more aggressively. By that time, approximately 15,000 people must have gathered. After that, the crowd began trying to break the barricade, throwing bottles, and tearing down the banner marking the restricted zone. During this, even after our team including myself persuaded the crowd, it was not ready to listen, and even when volunteers present there persuaded them, the crowd's agitation and aggression only grew further. Some time later, approximately 50–100 motorcycles in a rally came down from the TR overpass and merged with the crowd. After that, the crowd became even more agitated and aggressive. During this, while we tried hard to prevent the crowd from breaking the barricade, the crowd broke through and advanced toward the Parliament Building. Water cannon from Nepal Police was also used to spray water to stop the crowd. After the crowd broke the barricade and advanced toward the Parliament Building, we took duty outside the Citizen Investment Fund gate side of the Parliament Building as per the commander's orders. After that, the crowd began throwing stones at police and breaking Parliament Building walls. During this, the crowd threw excessive stones at our team including myself, and many police colleagues including my commander and myself had been injured. As they attempted to enter the Parliament Building through the gate where we were on duty, we tried to baton-charge below the knee to disperse the crowd. After many of us including myself had been heavily injured, we went inside the Parliament Building for approximately 45 minutes for primary treatment and after treatment resumed duty at the same position. They were also burning tires. During this, an Armed Police Force ambulance that came to rescue injured police personnel was also set on fire by some members of that crowd. After that, there was a confrontation between agitators and us for some time during which we used baton charges, gas guns, and rubber bullets. During this, 5 dummy rounds were used per commander's orders but we did not use live rounds. After that, how many rounds were fired from other teams and how many were injured  I could not determine anything about this. After that, the crowd continued breaking Parliament Building walls, climbing walls, and throwing stones at police. As the crowd near the Parliament Building thinned and congestion increased toward Everest Hospital, our team took duty toward Everest Hospital. 5.1.5 Statements and Incident Description Documents of Armed Police Force Nepal:
111. Statement of Armed Police Inspector General Raju Aryal:

Regular reporting to the organization chief to obtain information about the actual situation of any movement is done through the head of the Armed Police Force Headquarters Operations Department. Reporting and directive chains among the AIGP, DIGP, SSP, and SP levels have been maintained in accordance with the chain of command.

Prior to the movement on Bhadra 23, 2082, no reporting had been done through the Armed Police Force's intelligence gathering system and organizational structure about the social media platforms such as Reddit, Discord, and X being used by the Gen-Z youth generation. Although no concrete prior intelligence was received about plans to attack the Federal Parliament Building from the movement, based on analysis, following the movement and events at Tinkune on Chaitra 15 of the previous year, the Baneswhar area where the Federal Parliament Building is located had been designated as a high security challenge area. Instructions had been given through the Operations Department according to organizational structure to Armed Police Force Nepal commanders to analyze security challenges, adopt security alertness, formulate integrated security plans from all district security committees, and maintain effective coordination with other security agencies for security deployment. Prior to the Government of Nepal's decision to shut down social media, no opinion or advice had been sought from Armed Police Force Nepal regarding the security challenges that could arise from it.

During the course of the Bhadra 23 movement, while at the Home Ministry, he received information through the Operations Department that agitators were breaking through the restricted zone and coming toward the Federal Parliament Building. After assessing the situation, he gave directives through the Operations Department head for effective and coordinated security management. While still at the Home Ministry, he received information that demonstrators had broken through the security cordon and entered the Federal Parliament Building premises, and all security agency heads gave directives to their respective agencies to operate effectively and in a coordinated manner. As the situation became increasingly abnormal, after the curfew order issued by the District Administration Office Kathmandu, instructions were given to operate effectively in a coordinated manner with the District Security Committee / Chief District Officer and all security agencies according to the provisions of the Local Administration Act, following organizational structure.

Even as demonstrators threw stones, beat, and attacked security personnel and injured them, he had given instructions to the officers under him to fulfill their responsibilities in a restrained yet effective manner. Regarding coordination with the Nepali Army, he states that coordination was happening at the Prime Minister, Home Minister, and Home Secretary levels, and that he had maintained necessary information and coordination in his own capacity. He clarifies that the decision to fire was not made by him personally, and that field-deployed security personnel made necessary decisions based on law, SOP, and situational assessment. He claims that he did not receive any official report of lethal shooting at the crowd in violation of international police standards and human rights norms by the Armed Police Force, but claims aerial firing did occur. He states that all Armed Police Force personnel deployed at the Parliament Building premises were familiar with crowd control SOPs and that a Layered Defense Plan was also being implemented.

He clarifies that Armed Police Force Nepal was deployed as part of the integrated security plan per the District Security Committee's decision, not as a dedicated security force for the Federal Parliament Building, but was deployed to handle the immediate situation. According to him, field commanders kept the principle of 'life over property' at the center and adopted maximum restraint.

After the Bhadra 23 Federal Parliament Building incident, a security briefing for security chiefs was held with the Prime Minister. Discussing potential security challenges that could arise in Kathmandu and across the country from the second day, instructions were given to subordinate units to maintain high alertness, deploy necessary forces, protect and promote human rights, prevent further human casualties, adopt 'life over property,' keep contingency plans ready. Additionally, instructions were given to exercise restraint in use of force, ensure protection of human rights, and adhere to the principle of minimum use of force.

On the morning of Bhadra 24, they arrived at Prime Minister's residence Baluwatar. After informing the Prime Minister about crowd control and security challenges, arson, vandalism, and looting at public places, the Prime Minister acknowledged the seriousness of the incident and gave directives to bring greater effectiveness to coordination among security agencies.
He described the deadly attacks on security personnel and killings at various locations on Bhadra 24 as extremely condemnable and as a serious challenge to the state's security structure.

Regarding damage, looting of weapons and ammunition during security management, he states that a joint coordinated action plan among Armed Police Force Nepal, Nepal Police, Nepali Army, and district administration was immediately implemented, and search and recovery of looted weapons, ammunition, and prisoners who escaped from prisons is ongoing.

He confirmed that after the security briefing at Baluwatar on Bhadra 24, he along with other security agency chiefs arrived at the Jangi Adda via Nepali Army helicopter, discussed security management and coordination there, and returned to Armed Police Force Nepal Headquarters that same evening.
He states that the authority to order lethal force does not fall within his jurisdiction under the Local Administration Act and that he did not give any such order.

No Armed Police Force personnel died during the Bhadra 23 and 24 movement, but some were injured, and personal vehicles of Armed Police Force personnel, office supplies, and security equipment were also damaged or looted. In that movement, SLR 10 barrels, gas gun 4 barrels, and related ammunition went missing from Armed Police Force No. 1 Baraha Battalion Headquarters Sunsari; and SLR 11 barrels, gas gun 2 barrels, SMG 1 barrel, and related ammunition went missing from Armed Police Force No. 9 Pashupati Battalion Headquarters Kathmandu  reports to this effect have been received.

A list of security personnel who performed their duties courageously has been prepared and arrangements have been made to award them on Armed Police Day. An internal investigation committee has been formed for those who evaded responsibilities and showed weakness  after the report comes, necessary legal/disciplinary action will be taken.

He states that Armed Police Force Nepal security personnel operated professionally despite limited resources and manpower. In the course of maintaining professionalism, adverse circumstances were created. He states that the Armed Police Force did not fail in professionalism at any point.

In the latter part of his statement, he emphasizes that to prevent recurrence of such events in the future, administrative reform, human resource capacity development, regular training, adequate practice of non-lethal measures, sensitivity toward human rights protection, and preparedness are essential. He notes that to maintain high security personnel morale, career security, compensation, insurance, and social security assurance are necessary. He concludes that a neutral and professional security mechanism free from political interference is the long-term solution. Overall, Raju Aryal's statement presents the viewpoint that the events were not the result of intentional or standards-violating actions by the Armed Police Force, but rather the outcome of security management conducted within legal bounds under extremely complex and pressured circumstances.
112. Statement of Armed Police Additional Inspector General Narayandatta Paudel:

The initial intelligence provided by subordinate battalions about the demonstration organized by the Gen-Z group was that it was estimated to remain limited peacefully within the Mandala-New Baneswhar perimeter.
